question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply the equation by $-1$ to make the coefficient of the cubic term positive. This gives

$$
9{y}^{3}-27{y}^{2}-y+3=0.
$$

We then proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{3}-27{y}^{2}-y+3 & = \\ 9{y}^{2}(y-3)-1(y-3) & = \\ (9{y}^{2}-1)(y-3) & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(9{y}^{2}-1)(y-3)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(9{y}^{2}-1)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{1}{9} \\ y & =\pm \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $(y-3)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=3,\,\pm \frac{1}{3}.$
